messages:
support_jay: FYI customer A reported a big perf regression after yesterday's autoscale change — EU tenants are seeing p95 jump to ~1.2s and some 503s. Traces show requests going to hosted/us-east-1 rather than our eu-dedicated pool. billing spike too :grimacing:

mira: tenant id? any headers from their repro?

support_jay: tenant-456. They provided a curl repro and an SDK trace. They set region_hint=eu-west-1 and X-Redwood-Pin: tenant-456. Still routed to hosted. Paste of their curl:

```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" \ 
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \ 
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: tenant-456" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rw-large", "prompt":"hi"}'
```

infer_log snippet from their trace: `route_decision: fallback->hosted/us-east-1 reason=DEDICATED_FULL ttl_ms=0`

infra_raj: looking at routing records now. give me a min

infra_raj: seeing many entries where pin for tenant-456 points to eu-dedicated-2 but pool status=DEGRADED and pool_free_slots=0. fallback policy for that pool is overflow_to_hosted=true (configured q2 last month). That'll send to hosted if pool can't accept.

mira: who flipped overflow_to_hosted? that's aggressive for EU-sensitive customers.

infra_raj: change was part of autoscale tweak yesterday to avoid queueing under load. intention was global, but policy didn't respect region affinity for some pinned tenants.

eng_runtime_lee: can we reproduce locally with a pinned tenant? I'll attempt a repro by exhausting pool then sending requests with tenant header.

sre_anne: note: hosted fallback causes cross-region egress charges + much higher tail latency; ops alerted finance, saw hosted_requests for eu region spike 3x.

support_jay: customer also saw occasional auth errors 401 when routed to hosted. suspect token scope bound to dedicated routing key.

mira: steps to repro for eng: 1) create pin record for tenant-456 onto small eu-dedicated pool; 2) push load to consume all pool slots; 3) send single request with X-Redwood-Tenant: tenant-456 and X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 and observe route header in response.

eng_runtime_lee: doing that now. quick check: how to inspect pin TTL/owner?

infra_raj: use adminctl:
```
adminctl get-pin --tenant tenant-456 --json
# fields: pinned_pool, pinned_at, ttl_seconds, fallback_policy
```

eng_runtime_lee: repro confirms it: when pool_free_slots==0 router sets route.hosted and response header `x-redwood-route: hosted/us-east-1`. Also seeing `auth_hint: require_hosted_token` in logs which triggers 401s for the customer's dedicated-scoped tokens.

mira: OK immediate mitigation options?

infra_raj: short-term: flip overflow_to_hosted=false for eu-dedicated pools, set enqueue_policy=wait_with_backoff so requests queue locally instead of spilling. Risks: will increase latency briefly when queues back up, but avoids cross-region and auth mismatch.

eng_runtime_lee: I can push config change to a single eu pool as canary. will monitor realtime metrics.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-312 assigned to eng_runtime_lee, severity=P2, linked to billing alert 9876.

sre_anne: also recommend adding a router invariant: do not overflow pinned tenants to hosted unless tenant opt-in flag is set. that'll prevent tokens/auth mismatch.

mira: agreed. jira for invariant and deploy rollback flagged for next patch. I'll draft customer-facing message with mitigation steps: "we're pausing overflow for your tenant, requests will be queued briefly while we scale your dedicated pool".

support_jay: customer on Slack asked for repro steps; I'll send a sanitized version and ETA ~30m for canary.

eng_runtime_lee: canary change applied to eu-dedicated-2 at +20s. initial signs: hosted_requests for tenant-456 dropped to 0, p95 reduced to ~260ms. no auth 401s observed in the last 2 mins.

infra_raj: created temporary alert rule to fire if queue_latency > 800ms so we don't silently degrade.

mira: long-term followups: 1) router invariant to respect tenant pinning 2) restrict fallback_to_hosted for region-mismatched overflow 3) add pre-check in controller so pool scaling happens earlier for pinned tenants 4) add billing attribution for fallback events.

support_jay: I'll update the customer and keep thread. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: INC-2026-312 status=investigating, note="canary applied, monitoring"

mira: thanks everyone. once stable we'll backfill a postmortem and ship the invariant change.
